title: One noisy cellular automaton with an uncomputable noise diagram
description:
Can varying only the noise rate of one cellular automaton encode halting? We construct one computably specified finite-alphabet, finite-range automaton on Z^6 with computable disjoint rational open rate intervals I_n. Throughout I_n, uniform replacement noise makes it ergodic exactly when a fixed universal machine halts on n. Halting gives exponential all-input coalescence and attraction from every initial law; nonhalting gives at least two translation-invariant stationary laws and continuum many extremal stationary laws.

Hierarchical rulers select the input from the noise rate. Finite computation boards read the input; a threshold checker preserves a bit, and interval sensors erase every surviving chart when the computation halts. The space-time correspondence gives one fixed {0,1}-energy interaction on Z^7: on the corresponding temperature windows, halting gives one Gibbs measure and exponential weak spatial mixing in arbitrary volumes; nonhalting gives continuum many extremal Gibbs measures. These extremes need not be translation invariant. The zero-field pressure is analytic, yet its derivative in one fixed field direction exists at zero exactly on halting windows. Thus one fixed local rule has an uncomputable noise diagram.
notes: Preprint. It has not been peer reviewed. Version 1.1.0 updates version 1.0.0 (10.5281/zenodo.24147269). Corrections: the time-span and two-terminal clauses of Lemma 5.1, with the proof of Lemma 5.4 adjusted to them; the gate classification of Section 3.2, now restricted to finite bottom rows; the phase decoder of Section 3.2, which now uses finite approximants instead of liftability; the birth-contour clock in Lemma 8.4; and the helper-parent count in the proof of Proposition 2.1, which is B rather than B+1, with the parent bound kappa unchanged. Theorem A, Theorem 9.3, Corollary 9.4 and the construction constants are unchanged. Additions: Theorem 9.5, exponential all-input coalescence on halting windows, proved in Appendix A; Corollary B strengthened to exactly one Gibbs measure, with exponential weak spatial mixing, on halting windows, through Corollary 13.7 of our space-time paper, so that it answers Open problem 9.2 as well as Open problem 9.1 of our paper on an uncomputable phase diagram at positive temperature; Theorem 9.6, continuum many extremal stationary laws and Gibbs measures on nonhalting windows, not necessarily translation invariant; Theorem 9.7 and Corollary 9.8, an analytic zero-field pressure whose field derivative at zero exists exactly on halting windows; Theorem B.1, a computable robustness radius for local kernels; Corollaries 9.9-9.12, effective consequences; and Remark 9.13, sharper Chernoff scales that the construction does not use.
